description: Compact JWS (ES256, did:key) conformance vectors for packages/shared/src/jws.ts. testKey.privateKeyHex is TEST-ONLY — never used for anything but generating these fixtures. Signatures are single-hash RFC 7515 ES256 (@noble/curves p256.sign/verify called with { prehash: false } over sha256(signingInput) — the library's prehash:true default would double-hash and is NOT RFC 7515 ES256). valid[] entries must verifyCompact(jws, testKey.did) -> ok(payload). invalid[] entries must verifyCompact(jws, did) -> err(...) for the stated reason. Consumed by packages/shared/test/jws.test.ts; intended to be replayed by the web viewer against its own implementation (03-spec §3).

testKey.note: TEST-ONLY private key scalar. Never used in production.

invalid.name: bad-signature
invalid.reason: signature byte corrupted after signing (originally signed { action: 'exchange' })

invalid.name: tampered-payload
invalid.reason: payload segment replaced with { amount: 999999 } after signing { amount: 1 }; signature no longer matches

invalid.name: kid-did-mismatch
invalid.reason: JWS is validly signed by testKey but its kid says testKey.did; verifying it against an unrelated did (the identityDeep parity fixture DID) must fail the kid/did check

invalid.name: extra-header-key
invalid.reason: header is { alg: 'ES256', kid: testKey.did+'#0', crit: ['b64'] } — validly signed over this exact (non-conformant) signing input; verifyCompact must reject any header that isn't exactly {alg, kid} per RFC 7515 §4.1.11, not silently ignore the extra `crit` member

invalid.name: kid-wrong-fragment
invalid.reason: kid is testKey.did+'#1' instead of the only valid '#0' fragment (a did:key document has exactly one verification method); validly signed over this exact signing input, so this exercises the kid-exactness check specifically, not signature verification
